rounds.text: Vipul Organics Ltd trades at an exorbitant valuation that is completely detached from its underlying fundamental reality [E1, E70]. The stock commands a trailing P/E ratio of 73x and an EV/EBITDA of 29.06x, sitting well above sector benchmarks while offering a mediocre return on equity of just 7.6% [E1, E11, E13]. A discounted cash flow model values the intrinsic worth at a mere ₹ 40 per share against a market price of ₹ 265, resulting in an alarming margin of safety of -555.8% [E2, E44, E45]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's market price already demands an aggressive 25.9% earnings growth, which starkly contrasts with a stagnant 0% compounded profit growth over the past five years and poor 5-year sales growth of 7.97% [E19, E46, E60]. Free cash flow has deteriorated to ₹ -24 Cr in March 2026, and borrowings have escalated to ₹ 53 Cr alongside a flagged concern that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E36, E39, E62]. Compounded by a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -80.8% and high annualised volatility of 79.2%, the current price-led momentum hides deep structural and financial risks [E52, E53, E55]. Conceded: [E20], [E21], [E66].

The valuation is completely disconnected from underlying fundamentals, trading at an aggressive P/E of 73x and a P/B of 4.30x [E1, E2], while a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at just Rs 40 per share, resulting in a staggering -555.8% margin of safety [E44, E45]. Compounded profit growth over a 5-year period stands flat at 0%, and 3-year and 5-year median ROE figures languish at a weak 7%, proving that current pricing heavily outpaces actual historical earnings delivery [E13, E19, E27, E28, E55]. Furthermore, free cash flow has plunged to Rs -24 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside rising borrowings of Rs 53 Cr, and the company carries a history of extreme volatility with an annualized volatility of 79.2% and a terrifying worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -80.8% [E36, E39, E52, E53]. Conceded: [E20].
